Source of Income Discrimination — City of Fremont

On April 16, 2019, the City Council adopted the Source of Income Discrimination amendment to the Rent Review Ordinance, effective Thursday, May 16, 2019. Under this law, landlords can no longer discriminate against existing or potential tenants based on source of income. The amendment expands the definition of "source of income" to mean all lawful sources of income or rental assistance program, homeless assistance program, security deposit assistance program, or housing subsidy program, including the Housing Choice Voucher Program (Section 8).

Contact: Rent Review information line (510) 733-4945 or RentReview@Fremont.gov.

Source of Income Discrimination — Frequently Asked Questions, City of Fremont (revised 8.23.2019)

Who must comply? All housing providers who rent residential property in Fremont, except hotels, boarding houses, transient accommodations, dormitories, mobile homes, junior ADUs, and shared housing.

Can landlords advertise "I do not accept Section 8?" No — it is unlawful to make, print, publish, advertise, or disseminate any notice or advertisement indicating a tenant will be declined based on source of income.

How can a tenant with a subsidy meet minimum income requirements? If the applicant receives a governmental rent subsidy such as Section 8, landlords may only apply a minimum income requirement to the tenant's portion of the rent. Example: a landlord requiring income of three times the rent on a $2,000 unit, where the applicant has a $1,400 Section 8 voucher and pays $600 — the landlord may only require income of $1,800 (three times the tenant's portion), not $6,000.

Are landlords required to rent to anyone with a subsidy? Landlords cannot decline a tenant based only on source of income, but may still screen applicants on lawful criteria including credit and background checks; all Fair Housing laws still apply.

What about existing tenants? Landlords cannot interrupt or terminate a tenancy based on source of income, and cannot refuse to accept third-party subsidy payments for an existing tenant who becomes able to receive them.

Does the amendment restrict rent amounts? No — landlords may set rents as long as they follow federal, state, and local laws; the Rent Review Ordinance provides a non-binding dispute process.

What happens if a housing provider does not comply? The City may initiate enforcement including an administrative citation and monetary fine; tenants may also file a complaint in civil court seeking damages.

Prohibited actions based on source of income: interrupting or terminating tenancy; refusing to rent an available unit; refusing or restricting facilities, services, repairs, or improvements; publishing any discriminatory notice or advertisement; failing to account for third-party rental payments; failing to account for the aggregate income of persons residing together.

City of Fremont Rent Review Program, 3300 Capitol Avenue, Bldg. B, Fremont, CA 94538.
